title: The birthday deduction
prompt: Your boss's birthday is one of these ten dates: Mar 4, Mar 5, Mar 8, Jun 4, Jun 7, Sep 1, Sep 5, Dec 1, Dec 2, Dec 8.

He told you only the month, and told your colleague C only the day. Then you announced: "I don't know the birthday — and neither does C." Hearing this, C said: "I didn't know before, but now I do." You replied: "Now I know it too."
hints: For you to be certain C doesn't know, you must rule out any month where a unique day exists. Which days appear only once across all ten dates?
Days 2 and 7 each appear exactly once (Dec 2 and Jun 7). If C had been told either of those, C would already know the birthday. So your month must exclude both — ruling out June and December.
After your statement, C knows the month is March or September. Among those dates, C can now pinpoint the birthday. Which days appear more than once in March and September?
solution_lede:
Each statement in the conversation carries a logical constraint — strip away the drama and extract it.

Your confidence that C doesn't know means your month can't contain any day that uniquely identifies a birthday. Days 2 and 7 appear only once across all 10 dates (Dec 2, Jun 7). If your month were December or June, C might have been told 2 or 7 and would already know. So your month must be March or September.

C deduces the same thing from your statement and immediately knows the birthday. That means the day C was told is unique within the March/September subset: Mar 4, Mar 5, Mar 8, Sep 1, Sep 5. Days 4 and 5 each appear twice; day 1 appears once. C was told 1. The only match is Sep 1.

You, knowing the month is September, confirm it.

solution_steps.body: Find unique days across all 10 dates: day 2 (Dec 2) and day 7 (Jun 7) each appear only once.
Your certainty that C doesn't know rules out June and December — those months contain uniquely identifying days.
Remaining candidates: Mar 4, Mar 5, Mar 8, Sep 1, Sep 5. C now knows → the day must be unique here. Days 4 and 5 appear twice; day 1 appears once.
C was told day 1. The only match is Sep 1. You, knowing September, confirm.
